See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. Autonomous robots operating in open and changing environments must adapt not only what they know, but also how they think, learn, and interact when previously unseen situations arise. However, most existing approaches assume predefined reasoning, learning, or interaction mechanisms and mainly adapt knowledge or model parameters within these fixed structures. This paper proposes an open-ended cognitive evolution framework that maintains a minimal cognitive core while allowing concrete thinking, learning, and interaction methods to be selected, validated, reused, updated, and expanded according to observed evidence and accumulated experience. The framework also incorporates discrepancy-driven evaluation to detect when previously valid knowledge or capabilities have become outdated. Experiments over five independent seeds show that newly acquired thinking activities achieve 94.67% first-encounter success on unseen conflict families, with 98.67% reuse. Adaptive learning-method selection reaches 95.00% accuracy and improves task success to 69.16%, compared with 55.66% for the best fixed learner. Under unannounced environmental changes, the proposed method achieves 96.43% task success, only 1.07% hazard rate and 1.43% outdated decisions, while reducing verification operations by 48.0% relative to periodic updating.

Abstract
Agreement Technologies refer to open computer systems in which autonomous
software agents interact with one another, typically on behalf of humans, in order
to come to mutually acceptable agreements. With the advance of AI systems in
recent years, it has become apparent that such agreements, in order to be accept-
able to the involved parties, must remain aligned with ethical principles and
moral values. However, this is notoriously difficult to ensure, especially as differ-
ent human users (and their software agents) may hold different value systems,
i.e. they may differently weigh the importance of individual moral values. Fur-
thermore, it is often hard to specify the precise meaning of a value in a particular
context in a computational manner. Methods to estimate value systems based
on human-engineered specifications, e.g. based on value surveys, are limited in
scale due to the need for intense human moderation. In this article, we propose a
novel method to automaticallylearnvalue systems from observations and human
demonstrations. In particular, we propose a formal model of thevalue system
learningproblem, its instantiation to sequential decision-making domains based
on multi-objective Markov decision processes, as well as tailored preference-based
and inverse reinforcement learning algorithms to infer value grounding functions
